body:
## Pull request overview

This PR centralizes LLM provider auto-detection inside `AIServicePlugin`, removing duplicated adapter-selection logic from the CLI and adding test coverage to ensure the fallback/precedence behavior stays consistent across environments.

**Changes:**
- Added env-driven LLM adapter auto-detection to `AIServicePlugin` (with Memory fallback + logging).
- Updated CLI `serve` to rely on `AIServicePlugin` auto-detection instead of constructing adapters itself.
- Adjusted metadata package test wiring (Vitest aliases + driver-memory class rename) and added AI auto-detection tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/plugin.ts | Adds `detectAdapter()` and ensures plugin always configures an adapter (explicit > env-detected > memory), with logging. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/__tests__/ai-service.test.ts | Adds integration tests for adapter auto-detection behavior and logging. |
| packages/metadata/vitest.config.ts | Adds Vitest aliases needed for metadata tests (driver-memory + spec/api). |
| packages/metadata/src/metadata-history.test.ts | Updates driver-memory import/type from `MemoryDriver` to `InMemoryDriver`. |
| packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts | Removes CLI-side LLM adapter detection; always loads `AIServicePlugin()` and lets it detect. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Documents the new AIServicePlugin auto-detection behavior and env var priority. |
</details>

The final fallback warning is misleading when an env var is set but the provider SDK fails to load (or the factory export isn’t a function): it currently logs “No LLM provider configured via environment variables…”. Consider changing this to something like “No usable LLM provider could be initialized; falling back to MemoryLLMAdapter” and optionally include which provider/envKey was attempted so production logs are actionable (update the related test expectations accordingly).
